as_told.title: Princeton radar tracks over ten days before the Nimitz encounter

plain: In 2004, off San Diego, radar operators with the Navy carrier Nimitz are said to have tracked strange objects for days before a famous encounter with Navy pilots. Michels reads it this way: "The controller told us that these objects had been observed for over two weeks coming down from over 80,000 feet." A guest named Marik von Rennenkampff, crediting a man named Kevin Day, gives it as about 10 days, with "anomalous objects at 28,000 ft heading south at 100 knots, very strange tracks". The tellers raise it because it would mean the objects were being watched on radar long before anyone saw them with their eyes.
